basics.name: Julia Youssef
basics.label: Geophysical Sciences graduate
basics.summary: Recent UChicago Geophysical Sciences graduate with experience in paleontology, quantitative ecology, computational research, and scientific communication. Skilled in analyzing complex biological datasets, developing research workflows, and working with museum and fossil specimens.

courses: Course Highlights: Intro. To Python Prog. w/ Appl. to Astro Statistics, Phylogenetics, Biodiversity, Biogeochemical Cycles, Geobiology
Awards, Honors, Other: QuestBridge NCM Finalist, Odyssey Scholar, National Merit Scholar. Honors in Major.

work.name: Slater Lab - Multivariate Ecology on Mammalian Herbivores
highlights: Developed computational pipelines, structured datasets, and informed models for comparative ecology and phylogenetic research

Herbivory: Built literature review and data-extraction workflows to characterize diet in mammalian herbivores as a multivariate ecological trait for use in predictive models using dental morphology; applied PCA and clustering analyses to identify different subniches and specialist guilds

Pterosaur Phylogeny: Compared morphological datasets and phylogenetic methods using parsimony, Bayesian inference, and fossil occurrence data to investigate persistent topological disagreements; developed scripts for PBDB, tree processing, and cross-dataset analysis

work.name: PhoenixFarms NFP
highlights: Contribute to development and maintenance of a community Food Forest supplying produce to local food pantry
Planned grant-funded planting of 12 fruit and nut trees, developing an ecologically informed site-plan based on canopy size, light, species interactions, and long-term management
Built site infrastructure and created public-facing FAQs for community partners and volunteers

work.name: Sereno Fossil Lab
work.dateText: Sept. 2021 - Dec. 2024, Summer Tech Jun. - Aug. 2023, Jul. 2026 - Current
highlights: Prepared fossil vertebrate specimens, as well as creating visualizations, diagrams, and casts for display, outreach, and donor gifts
Participated in small, week-long expedition to exposed Morrison, Cloverly formations at base of Bighorn Mountains, involving excavating and stabilizing dinosaur fossils (Camarasaurus vertebra)

work.name: Eodiscid Trilobite Fossil Processing & Morphological Analysis
highlights: Cleaned, stained, and photographed dozens of mm-scale eodiscid trilobites for morphological analysis and use in biostratigraphy

work.name: Liew House Dorm Resident Assistant

work.name: Deep Skies Lab
highlights: Utilized simulation-based-inference to analyze the relationships between cosmological constraints, dark matter halos in galaxy clusters, and the observed SZ effect in the cosmic microwave background
Used regression and classification machine learning techniques in cosmological and astrophysical applications; presented research to Deep Skies collaborators and Fermilab
